title: The Real Cost of a Lamborghini Revuelto (Options, Taxes, Insurance)

scenes.text: In October twenty twenty-six, a Lamborghini Revuelto test car left the press fleet with a window sticker of eight hundred six thousand five hundred twenty-one dollars. The base price was about six hundred sixty-five thousand. The rest was options, delivery, and a tax most people do not expect on a plug-in hybrid. So what does a Revuelto really cost, from the order form to the day you sell it?
scenes.caption: THE REAL COST OF A REVUELTO

scenes.text: Today we go line by line. The base price and how it climbed, the options that cost more than a normal car, the taxes, the insurance, the fuel, the service, and the used market, where something unusual is happening. Then we add it all up, using only published numbers.
scenes.caption: LINE BY LINE

scenes.text: Every figure in this video has a source in the description. Some come from window stickers, some from price guides, some from insurers, and when a number is our own simple example, we will say so. With a car like this, the details are where the money hides.
scenes.caption: EVERY NUMBER IS SOURCED

scenes.text: And here is the first twist. The price of a Revuelto went up while it was already sold out. Let's start at the beginning.
scenes.caption: THE PRICE KEPT CLIMBING

scenes.text: When the Revuelto was revealed in March twenty twenty-three, Lamborghini had not announced American pricing. Motor Authority reported that in other markets it started at about five hundred thousand euros, roughly five hundred forty-nine thousand dollars at the time. By July twenty twenty-three, before a single car was delivered, the production for the next two years was already allocated.
scenes.caption: ABOUT €500,000 TO START

scenes.text: In the United Kingdom, Supercars dot net reported a base price of four hundred fifty thousand pounds in twenty twenty-three, about five hundred seventy-five thousand dollars at the time. And it showed how fast that number grows. One customer's configured car came to about five hundred fifty thousand pounds, and another dealer's example reached about five hundred ninety thousand pounds.
scenes.caption: £450,000 BECOMES £590,000

scenes.text: In the United States, the base price kept rising. Kelley Blue Book lists a starting sticker of about six hundred seventy-three thousand dollars for the twenty twenty-six Revuelto. Jalopnik's twenty twenty-six test car had a base price of six hundred sixty-four thousand seven hundred ninety-nine dollars. Either way, the entry ticket in America is well above six hundred and fifty thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: ~$665,000 TO $673,000 BASE

scenes.text: Here is the twist. Rising prices did not slow demand. Lamborghini delivered a record ten thousand six hundred eighty-seven cars in twenty twenty-four, according to duPont Registry, and Wikipedia lists one thousand four hundred six Revueltos built that year. When a car is sold out, the maker sets the price, not the buyer.
scenes.caption: SOLD OUT, SO PRICES ROSE

scenes.text: Before we count the costs, let's be clear about what the money buys. A six point five liter naturally aspirated V12 with about eight hundred fourteen horsepower, three electric motors, and a total of one thousand and one horsepower. Zero to one hundred kilometers per hour in two point five seconds, and a top speed of about two hundred seventeen miles per hour, according to Wikipedia.
scenes.caption: WHAT $665,000 BUYS

scenes.text: It also buys a car that experts rate highly. In Top Gear's twenty twenty-five Performance Car of the Year, the Revuelto beat the Ferrari twelve Cilindri and the Aston Martin Vanquish on track, and the writer said its chassis can keep pace with its engine. So the price is not only for the badge. It is for one of the best-reviewed V12 cars on sale.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR'S TRACK WINNER

scenes.text: And it buys rarity, at least for now. A car that was sold out for two years before deliveries, built largely by hand in Sant'Agata Bolognese. Keep that in mind, because rarity is the reason some of the numbers later in this video look so strange.
scenes.caption: BUILT BY HAND IN SANT'AGATA

scenes.text: Now, line by line, here is what that ticket really costs.
scenes.caption: LINE BY LINE

scenes.text: Now options, where Lamborghini makes a lot of its money. Jalopnik published the full option list of its twenty twenty-six test car, painted in Viola thirtieth. Total options came to one hundred thirty-three thousand two hundred twenty-seven dollars. That is more than many new Porsches cost.
scenes.caption: $133,227 IN OPTIONS

scenes.text: The biggest items were two carbon fiber packages. A lower exterior carbon pack, with the front splitter, side skirts, rear diffuser, and bumper fins, cost twenty-four thousand six hundred twenty-three dollars. An upper exterior carbon pack, with the windshield surround, mirrors, door handles, side intakes, and engine cover, cost twenty-five thousand nine hundred seventy-eight.
scenes.caption: TWO CARBON PACKS: $50,601

scenes.text: Together, those two packs cost fifty thousand six hundred one dollars. Jalopnik pointed out that this is more than the average transaction price of a new car in America, which Kelley Blue Book put at fifty thousand five hundred sixty-two dollars in September twenty twenty-six. The carbon trim alone costs more than the car most Americans drive.
scenes.caption: MORE THAN AN AVERAGE NEW CAR

scenes.text: The rest of the list is a lesson in how small things add up. The paint was fourteen thousand three hundred thirty-one dollars. Silver stripes on the diffuser were four thousand fifty-two. Gray stitching was six thousand ninety-two. Sport seats were eight thousand three hundred eighty-seven. The Sonus faber audio system was six thousand six hundred twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: PAINT: $14,331

scenes.text: Even features most cars include were options. The passenger display was four thousand fifty-two dollars. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto were three thousand seven hundred seventeen dollars. A parking pack was three thousand five hundred ninety-six. And an integrated garage door opener was six hundred seventy-one dollars. Black brake calipers were one thousand nine hundred fifty-nine.
scenes.caption: CARPLAY: $3,717

scenes.text: Here is the twist. Those are the standard options. Lamborghini also offers Ad Personam, its personalization program, and Supercars dot net reported that Ad Personam options can cost one hundred thousand pounds or more. A unique paint color or a custom interior can push a Revuelto toward a million dollars.
scenes.caption: AD PERSONAM: £100,000+

scenes.text: At the very top of the market are the one-off cars. Lamborghini's Ad Personam department has built Revuelto Opera Unica cars with hand-painted liveries and custom interiors, including one inspired by the Taurus constellation and one inspired by Sardinia, according to Wikipedia. Those cars have no public price, and that is part of the point. When a car is unique, the price is whatever the buyer and Lamborghini agree on.
scenes.caption: ONE-OFFS HAVE NO PRICE TAG

scenes.text: Then come the fees. Jalopnik's sticker included a destination charge of three thousand nine hundred ninety-five dollars, which is the cost of delivering the car to the dealer. And it included a gas guzzler tax of four thousand five hundred dollars.
scenes.caption: $3,995 DESTINATION

scenes.text: The gas guzzler tax is a federal tax on cars with low fuel economy. And here is the twist. The Revuelto is a plug-in hybrid, but it still pays it. Kelley Blue Book lists its fuel economy at ten miles per gallon in the city, seventeen on the highway, and twelve combined. The small battery is for performance, not for saving fuel.
scenes.caption: A HYBRID THAT PAYS A GUZZLER TAX

scenes.text: After that, there is sales tax, which depends on the state. As a simple example of our own, a seven percent sales tax on an eight hundred thousand dollar car would be fifty-six thousand dollars. That is another new pickup truck, just in tax. Registration fees in some states are also based on the value of the car.
scenes.caption: EXAMPLE: $56,000 IN SALES TAX

scenes.text: So before the car turns a wheel, the real price of a well-optioned Revuelto in America can be well above eight hundred thousand dollars, and close to nine hundred thousand with tax in many states. That is the true starting line for ownership.
scenes.caption: CLOSE TO $900,000 ON THE ROAD

scenes.text: Now insurance. MoneyGeek's August twenty twenty-six analysis estimated full coverage for a Revuelto at about five hundred thirty-nine dollars a month, for a forty-year-old driver with a clean record, good credit, and twelve thousand miles a year. Over twelve months, that is about six thousand four hundred sixty-eight dollars, which is our multiplication.
scenes.caption: ABOUT $539 A MONTH

scenes.text: That sounds surprisingly low for an eight hundred thousand dollar car. And here is the twist. MoneyGeek's same methodology produced a Bugatti Chiron estimate of about three thousand fifty-six dollars a month. These are model-based estimates from standard insurers, and MoneyGeek itself notes that exotic specialty insurers may quote very differently.
scenes.caption: AN ESTIMATE, NOT A QUOTE

scenes.text: In real life, insurance for a car like this depends on where it lives, how it is stored, how much it is driven, and the owner's history. Many owners use collector or exotic policies with agreed values and mileage limits. The honest answer is that a Revuelto can cost a few thousand dollars a year to insure, or much more.
scenes.caption: IT DEPENDS ON THE OWNER

scenes.text: And the Revuelto has one insurance risk that most cars do not have. Its doors. In twenty twenty-five, Lamborghini recalled twenty-seven United States cars because some pins on the door gas springs were installed incorrectly. A door could drop with force, or become hard to open from inside. Dealers fixed it free. But expensive, complex parts are exactly what makes repairs costly after an accident.
scenes.caption: COMPLEX PARTS, COSTLY REPAIRS

scenes.text: Fuel is the easy part to calculate. Kelley Blue Book lists twelve miles per gallon combined and a twenty-two point five gallon tank, on premium fuel. As our own example, if premium costs five dollars a gallon, one full tank costs about one hundred twelve dollars and fifty cents, and takes you roughly two hundred seventy miles in mixed driving.
scenes.caption: ONE TANK: ~$112

scenes.text: If an owner drives three thousand miles a year at twelve miles per gallon, that is two hundred fifty gallons, or about one thousand two hundred fifty dollars at five dollars a gallon. Again, that is our example. Compared with the price of the car, fuel is close to a rounding error.
scenes.caption: EXAMPLE: ~$1,250 A YEAR

scenes.text: And the battery helps a little. Kelley Blue Book lists a charge time of about two hours on a two hundred forty volt outlet, and Wikipedia lists about ten kilometers, or six miles, of electric range on the European test. For a short drive in the city, an owner can use the Citta mode and burn no fuel at all.
scenes.caption: 6 MILES ON ELECTRIC

scenes.text: Now service, and this is where Lamborghini is less open than you might expect. Kelley Blue Book lists a warranty of three years with unlimited miles for both basic and powertrain coverage. But Lamborghini does not publish a public price list for Revuelto servicing in the sources we could find.
scenes.caption: 3-YEAR UNLIMITED-MILE WARRANTY

scenes.text: Even dealers that advertise fixed-price servicing do not always show the numbers. H R Owen in the United Kingdom, one of the biggest Lamborghini dealers, lists its fixed-price services for the Huracan and Aventador as price on application, and does not list the Revuelto at all. You have to ask.
scenes.caption: PRICE ON APPLICATION

scenes.text: Some websites publish estimates for Revuelto servicing, but the ones we found gave no sources or methods, so we are not quoting them as facts. What we can say is that a Revuelto combines a V12, three electric motors, a high-voltage battery, carbon-ceramic brakes, and active aerodynamics. Each one needs specialist tools and training.
scenes.caption: NO RELIABLE PUBLIC PRICES

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The hybrid system may actually help with some wear. The front motors recover energy when slowing down, which can take some load off the brakes. And the new dual-clutch gearbox replaces the Aventador's single-clutch robotized unit, which reviewers often criticized. But the battery adds a component that the Aventador never had.
scenes.caption: HYBRID HELPS, AND ADDS

scenes.text: The brakes alone show the scale. Wikipedia lists carbon-ceramic discs of four hundred ten millimeters at the front with ten-piston calipers, and three hundred ninety at the rear. Carbon-ceramic brakes last a long time with normal use, but when they need replacing, they are among the most expensive parts on any car.
scenes.caption: 10-PISTON CALIPERS

scenes.text: Now the part where the Revuelto surprises people. Most cars lose a big part of their value in the first two years. In October twenty twenty-six, autoevolution looked at a twenty twenty-four Revuelto with about six thousand miles, offered for six hundred twenty-nine thousand nine hundred eighty dollars.
scenes.caption: 2 YEARS OLD: $629,980

scenes.text: The same article said used Revueltos start around six hundred thousand dollars and can reach almost nine hundred thousand, depending on mileage, condition, and options. For early cars, that is not far from their original sticker. In other words, a buyer who got an early allocation has often lost little, if any, value on paper.
scenes.caption: USED: $600K TO $900K

scenes.text: Why? Partly because the car was sold out for years, so people who could not get an allocation paid a premium to skip the line. Motor Authority reported back in twenty twenty-three that the only alternatives were waiting or paying hefty markups on the used market. Scarcity protects value.
scenes.caption: SCARCITY PROTECTS VALUE

scenes.text: But here is the twist. A new, faster version now exists. In August twenty twenty-six, Lamborghini revealed the Revuelto S V, with about one thousand fifty-one horsepower, eighty percent more downforce, and a Hockenheim lap record for production cars, according to Auto123. Motor1 reported a United States order sheet price of seven hundred forty-one thousand one hundred seventy-two dollars before options.
scenes.caption: THE SV: $741,172

scenes.text: When a faster version arrives, the regular car can lose some of its shine on the used market. On the other hand, the S V is limited to one thousand nine hundred sixty-three cars, mostly for existing customers. That could keep demand for regular Revueltos strong among buyers who could never get an S V. Nobody can promise which way it goes.
scenes.caption: NOBODY CAN PROMISE

scenes.text: Now a question most videos skip. How do people actually pay for a car like this? Many buyers at this level pay cash. But some finance, or lease, to keep their money invested elsewhere. Let's do a clearly simple example of our own, using round numbers, to show what financing a Revuelto would look like.
scenes.caption: HOW DO PEOPLE PAY?

scenes.text: Take a car at about eight hundred sixty thousand dollars on the road. Put twenty percent down, which is one hundred seventy-two thousand dollars. Finance the remaining six hundred eighty-eight thousand over seventy-two months at an example rate of seven percent. The monthly payment comes out to about eleven thousand seven hundred thirty dollars.
scenes.caption: EXAMPLE: $11,730 A MONTH

scenes.text: Over six years, the interest alone in that example adds up to about one hundred fifty-six thousand five hundred dollars. That is more than the total cost of the options on Jalopnik's test car. So for a financed buyer, the loan can cost more than the carbon fiber, the paint, and the audio system combined.
scenes.caption: INTEREST: ~$156,500

scenes.text: And for cash buyers, there is a hidden cost too. Money in a car is money not earning anything elsewhere. As another simple example, if eight hundred sixty thousand dollars could earn four percent a year in a savings product, that would be about thirty-four thousand four hundred dollars a year. Economists call that an opportunity cost.
scenes.caption: EXAMPLE: $34,400 A YEAR NOT EARNED

scenes.text: Here is the twist. With a car that holds its value well, like many early Revueltos, the opportunity cost can be the biggest yearly cost of all, bigger than insurance, fuel, and service together. The car may not lose much value, but the money inside it is not growing.
scenes.caption: THE BIGGEST YEARLY COST?

scenes.text: To guess the Revuelto's future, look at the car it replaced. The Aventador was built from twenty eleven to twenty twenty-two, and reports at the end of its run put production at about eleven thousand four hundred sixty-five cars. That is a lot of V12 Lamborghinis, and it meant that used Aventadors became much easier to find than new ones were to order.
scenes.caption: 11,465 AVENTADORS

scenes.text: The Revuelto is built in much smaller numbers per year. Wikipedia lists one thousand four hundred six in twenty twenty-four. If production stays at a similar pace over a long life, the total could still be large. And the larger the total, the more the used market behaves like a normal luxury car market over time.
scenes.caption: HOW MANY WILL BE BUILT?

scenes.text: The lesson is simple. Short-term values are protected by waiting lists. Long-term values depend on how many cars are built and how they are remembered. The Revuelto is the first hybrid V12 Lamborghini, which may help it be remembered. But no source can tell you what it will be worth in ten years.
scenes.caption: FIRST HYBRID V12: A COLLECTIBLE?

scenes.text: So let's add it up for one example car, using the numbers in this video. Jalopnik's test car came to eight hundred six thousand five hundred twenty-one dollars, including options, destination, and the gas guzzler tax. Add an example seven percent sales tax, and the car is around eight hundred sixty thousand dollars on the road.
scenes.caption: ~$860,000 ON THE ROAD

scenes.text: Add insurance at MoneyGeek's estimate of about six thousand five hundred dollars a year, fuel of around one thousand two hundred fifty dollars a year in our example, and service at whatever the dealer quotes. Over three years, the running costs we can document are in the tens of thousands of dollars, small next to the price of the car.
scenes.caption: RUNNING COSTS: TENS OF THOUSANDS

scenes.text: And then the biggest number, depreciation, may be smaller than for a normal luxury car. If a two-year-old car can sell for around six hundred thirty thousand dollars, the loss compared with a base price in the mid six hundreds could be modest. But options rarely hold their value. Those carbon packs and that special paint are worth far less to the next buyer.
scenes.caption: OPTIONS DON'T HOLD VALUE

scenes.text: So the real cost of a Revuelto is not mainly fuel or insurance. It is the options you choose and the timing of when you buy and sell. An early buyer with a simple spec can lose very little. A late buyer with a heavy spec who sells after the S V arrives could lose a lot.
scenes.caption: TIMING IS THE REAL COST

scenes.text: And then there is the Ferrari alternative. Kelley Blue Book lists the Ferrari twelve Cilindri from four hundred seventy-two thousand dollars, about two hundred thousand less than a Revuelto. We compare the two in detail in another video of this series.
scenes.caption: THE FERRARI: ~$200,000 LESS

scenes.text: Tell us in the comments: would you spend fifty thousand dollars on carbon fiber, or put that money into a whole second car? And watch the rest of this Revuelto series, two secrets hidden inside it, the Ferrari comparison, and the story of why Lamborghini built it this way.
scenes.caption: CARBON OR A SECOND CAR?

scenes.text: If your next purchase is a little more down to earth, our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality for more honest numbers about the cars and trucks people really talk about.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
